verses.text: Family, I’m talking to people who know the Law: it only has authority over someone while they’re alive, right?
For example, a married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives. If he dies, she’s released from that marriage law.
So if she joins another man while her husband’s still alive, people will call her an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she’s free from that law and isn’t an adulteress if she marries someone else.
Same idea for you, family: through Christ’s body, you died to the Law so you could belong to someone else—to Christ, who was raised from the dead. Now we can bear fruit for God.
When we lived by the flesh, sinful desires stirred up through the Law were at work in us, producing fruit that led to death.
But now we’ve been released from the Law, because we died to what held us. We can serve in the Spirit’s new way, not under the old written code.
So is the Law sin? Absolutely not! I wouldn’t have recognized sin if the Law hadn’t shown me. I wouldn’t have known what coveting was if the Law hadn’t said, “Don’t covet.”
But sin used that command as an opening and stirred up every kind of coveting in me. Without the Law, sin is lifeless.
There was a time I felt alive without the Law. Then the command came, sin woke up, and I died.
The command meant to bring life ended up bringing death for me.
Sin used the command to trick me—and through it, sin killed me.
So the Law is holy, and the command is holy, right, and good.
Did something good bring death to me? No way! Sin did it, using what was good to show itself for what it is. The command exposed sin as seriously sinful.
We know the Law is spiritual, but I’m human, sold under sin.
I don’t even understand my own actions. I don’t do what I want to do; I keep doing the thing I hate.
If I’m doing what I don’t want, I’m agreeing that the Law is good.
So it’s not the real me wanting this, but sin living in me.
I know nothing good lives in me—that is, in my flesh. I want to do what’s right, but I can’t seem to carry it out.
The good I want to do, I don’t do. The evil I don’t want—that’s what I keep practicing.
If I do what I don’t want, it’s no longer the real me choosing it; sin is living in me.
So this is the pattern I keep finding: when I want to do good, evil is right there too.
Deep inside, I delight in God’s Law,
but I see another law at work in my body, fighting the law my mind agrees with and dragging me into sin’s captivity.
I’m in a mess—who’s going to rescue me from this body headed for death?
Thank God—rescue comes through Jesus Christ our Lord! So with my mind I serve God’s Law, but with my flesh I serve sin’s law.
